finding.claim: Unauthenticated SSRF: /preview fetches any URL supplied by the caller and returns the status code and the first 500 characters of the response body. The attacker can reach internal services, localhost, and cloud metadata endpoints (e.g. http://169.254.169.254/) and read the responses.
finding.source: request.args.get('url') at app.py:15 (query parameter 'url' on GET /preview)
finding.sink: requests.get(target, timeout=5) at app.py:16, which follows redirects by default; the body is returned in the JSON response at app.py:17

trace.note: Route /preview registered with no authentication decorator or middleware
target = request.args.get('url', '') takes the attacker-controlled value
requests.get(target) is called with no scheme, host, or IP validation
resp.status_code and resp.text[:500] are returned to the attacker, so this is non-blind SSRF

finding.guards_checked: No allowlist, no scheme check, no private/link-local IP block, no auth check, and no redirect restriction. The only control is timeout=5, which is not an SSRF control. Sibling route /partner (app.py:23-25) has a hostname allowlist, but /preview has none.

verdict.reason: app.py:15 takes the attacker-controlled `url` query parameter and passes it straight to requests.get at app.py:16 with no auth, scheme, host or IP check (the ALLOWED_HOSTS check at app.py:23-24 applies only to /partner), and app.py:17 returns the status and the first 500 characters of the body.
